notes.body: - **New entrance sounds** (the designer's): Spiders have their own; male Soldiers and Warriors arrive with a salute (two takes); Knights and Paladins without Movement 3 clank in plate armour (those with 3 still ride in); Spirits that are not Darkness arrive with a friendly sound; dogs and big cats have a second take.

- **Summons with the same name are numbered in the order they entered.** Four Goblin Squires read "Goblin Squire 1" to "Goblin Squire 4" - in the log, on the board and in the detail view - so you can tell which one did what. A Summon alone of its name keeps its plain name; numbers are not reused in a game.
- **Seven Traps could never be set off, and now can:** Venomous Harvest, Tribute Demanded, Burning Crater, Conversion Trap, Caught in the Web, Roused from the Den and You Are Not Welcome. Their effects worked, but stepping on them never asked. A new check fails the build if another Trap is ever left in that state.

- **Archangels' Blessing is reworked** to the designer's new card: [2][1 Light], Universal. When an enemy Summon steps (or flies) onto its field, return a Summon from your graveyard that costs no more than it - to your Guarded Zone or right beside the intruder. **Avert [1 Light]:** when a Summon of yours would perish, it persists instead - it stays at 1 Life, depleted and deactivated. Battle deaths count; a sacrifice does not.
- **New faces from the designer's art** for 52 cards that had hand-made faces or art that had to be replaced - among them Combat Angel, Exalted Valkyrie, Soldier of Light, Spellblade Templar, Siege Master, Kanuz, Bymere, Cassiodor, City Guard and Divine Punisher - and new board pictures for many Light Summons.

- **New art:** Channel Fire, Destroy Defenses, Dominating Violence, Garl and Romuden now have faces drawn from the designer's art, and the Goblin Squire token has a face at all. New Permanents-box pictures for Hedrex, Cragtooth Slinger Chief, Scalding Tar and Blessing of Might, and a board picture for the Goblin Squire.
- **Channel Fire's face shows its copy limit (2)** again.

- **Incessant Rage kills its wearer when its Onslaught takes the last Life.** "Loses 2 life" left a 2-Life Summon standing at 0. Grimy Slaughterer's "loses 1 life" had the same gap.
- **The computer puts Incessant Rage on its own Summons** - it treated the card as removal for yours - and never on one of its own the first attack would kill.
- **Elemental Core: click the Item to sacrifice** in your Permanents box, instead of picking it in a window. When a Core can't be used, it now says why (already used this turn, nothing to sacrifice, no free field in your Guarded Zone, or not enough Energy) - each Core has its own [A].
- **Gnitharr: click a Summon on the board** for each Grit Counter, instead of a window.
- **Smuggler's Run shows its board art** on the column it covers.
- **Flaming Daggers has new art.**

- **Thurgan's look that finds no Equipment opens once.** The reveal of the top cards came up a second time over the first - black backdrop on black backdrop - and one copy stayed after you closed it. The game took the reveal for a lost question and asked it again. The same could happen to other reveals that answer a card (a hand shown by a card's effect).
- **An Intervene Item lights your own Permanents box.** Selected on your opponent's turn, The Fallen Feather (or any Item or Terrain you may cast then) made your opponent's box glow instead of yours.

- **Ysmera's Idyll is the designer's new list** (60 cards, 18 Pearl Collectors; Longwhisker, Maw of the Trench, Meditate, Message in a Bottle, End Fate and the Treasures Hidden Clear Spring, The Endless Deep and Lacurath). Against the other 51 pre-cons it won 38% of 306 games to the old list's 25%. The old list is kept as a saved deck, "Ysmera's Idyll (previous)".

- **The computer builds Siege Foundry before it casts its Equipment**, so the Equipment gets the Foundry's discount. It cast its Items first, and the Items spent the Energy the Foundry needed: Thurgan held it in more than half the games it drew it.
